parole.testo: Unknown. Probably from multiple sources; the sense "treasure" could ultimately be via rhotacism from Proto-Germanic *azaniz (“harvest”), *azniz, while the sense "giant" could ultimately be from Proto-Norse [Term?].
Possibly borrowed from (a descendant of) Proto-Germanic *aiþǭ (“legal, real wife”), from *aiþaz (“oath”).

parole.significato: line, long line; the longer fiber(s) of flax, hemp, etc.; heckled flax/hemp
parole.testo: Uncertain; possibly from Proto-Germanic *aiwīnaz (“everlasting”). The other Finnic terms (Ingrian aivina, Karelian aivina, Votic aivinõ) probably derive from Finnish.
Possibly ultimately from Proto-Germanic *aljaną.

parole.motivo_incerta: Uncertain; Unclear; Possibly; perhaps; modello unc/uncertain
parole.testo: Uncertain. Traditionally a western Finnish dialectal word; no known cognates exist in other Finnic languages. Possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *aldaz ~ *alþijaz (“old”) (for the ending, compare tyyris < *diurijaz; for the gradation, compare raitis << *raidi(ja)z), but the semantics are unclear;

parole.significato: to con, swindle, cheat, trick, deceive, hoax, defraud
parole.testo: Uncertain, has sometimes been theorized to be a borrowing from Proto-Germanic *swīkwaną (suggesting derivation through Proto-Finnic *huigat'ak, although no other Finnic cognates are known). Compare huikata, huikkia (“to barter”).

parole.significato: a long crack in a tree
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hoola + -ma, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hōlō.

Proto-Finnic *inta + -o (compare dialectal inta, Estonian ind, Livonian ind), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (compare Old Swedish inna (“achievement, accomplishment”)). Alternatively, a Uralic origin has been proposed. Compare Komi-Zyrian ӧд (öd, “speed”).
Possibly from the same root as kaiho; kaih- + -i, or more likely, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *haihaz.

parole.significato: detestation, abhorrence (feeling of strong fear and disgust)
parole.testo: Possibly an irregular derivation from the same root as kamala (for the m ~ mm variation, compare hämmentää < hämätä). Alternatively, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skamō (compare dialectal kamo), or from variant *skammō (whence Old Norse skǫmm).

parole.significato: manure (fertilizer made of animal excrement and urine)
parole.testo: Variant of lansi (“low-lying land”), possibly by backformation from dialectal lantea (“fertile, of land”). Semantic development has probably been through "fertile soil, material used as fertilizer". Attested since the early 18th century. A connection has also been purported to Proto-Germanic *hlandą

parole.significato: to spread, multiply; to grow stronger (particularly of skin conditions)
parole.testo: Unknown. Cognates include Karelian lautuo, Lule Sami lawˈdâ (“dispersed”) and lawˈdât (“to spread, disperse”). Possibly from Proto-Germanic *laudaz (“great”), perhaps with + -tua; compare lauti (“dispersed”), as well as Gothic *𐌻𐌰𐌿𐌸𐍃 (*lauþs, “great”) and 𐌻𐌹𐌿𐌳𐌰𐌽 (liudan, “to grow”).
maha (“belly, stomach”) + Proto-Finnic *paita (“caul”), the latter component borrowed from Proto-Germanic *faitaz.

parole.significato: expressing flattery or cuteness that is probably not sincere, unctuous, flattering
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *mairis + -ea, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *smairjaz.
melt- + -o. The root is probably borrowed from a descendant of Proto-Germanic *smeltaną (“to melt”), such as Old Norse *smelta or Old Swedish smælta.

From nav- + -akka, probably derived from the dialectal adjective navea with the same meaning. It has been proposed to be a borrowing from Proto-Germanic *snawwiz (“short-haired”), with a possibly secondary meaning of "fast"; this would imply a Proto-Finnic *navëda. Compare rivakka, ravakka.

parole.significato: to be barely visible, to be in sight
parole.testo: Proto-Finnic [Term?] + -ttaa, with the root borrowed from Proto-Germanic *blikaz.
Proto-Finnic *pullas + -ea, root borrowed from Proto-Germanic *fullaz (“full”).
Probably a variant of lonkka, but it is not known which is original. Origin from Proto-Germanic *wranhō (“angle, corner”) is also possible, but is rejected by LÄGLOS.

parole.significato: haycock (small, conical stack of hay left in a field to dry before adding to a haystack)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ruka + -o, borrowed either from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (whence Icelandic hrúga) or alternatively Proto-Germanic [Term?] (whence Old Norse hroki (“heap, pile”)). Cognate with Karelian ruko and dialectal Estonian ruga.

parole.significato: trunk (usually single, more or less upright part of a tree)
parole.testo: Proto-Finnic *runka + -o, the root borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skrunkaz (compare Icelandic skrokkur).
Uncertain. Possibly ultimately from Proto-Germanic *brutą, either through Proto-Finnic or through a Samic language.
The adessive singular of *tarjo, either from tarita (“to offer”) (archaic) + -o or alternatively separately borrowed from Proto-Germanic *tarjō.

Unknown. Possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *stīfaz (~ *stīfijaz?) (“stiff, rigid”) (compare other Germanic borrowings like tyyris < *diurijaz, raitis < *raidi(ja)z), implying Proto-Finnic *tiibis ~ *tiivis (without any Finnic cognates). In this case, the original sense would have been “tight, co

parole.significato: futile, in vain (incapable of producing results)
parole.testo: Unknown. Cognate with Ingrian turha and Kukkuzi turha. De Smit proposes borrowing from Proto-Germanic *þwerhaz (“cross, adverse, obstinate”).
From Proto-Finnic *turka + -nen, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *dwergaz.

parole.significato: to stay up, stay awake (to remain awake, to not go to bed)
parole.testo: Proto-Finnic *valvadak + -oa (the base verb valvaa is only found in dialects). Cognate to Estonian valvama and Karelian valvuo. Possibly further related to valaa, or borrowed from Proto-Germanic *walwijaną.

parole.significato: to look out for, watch out for, beware of; (with verbs) avoid (accidentally)
parole.testo: Probably vara (“caution, concern, care”) + -oa. May also be more directly borrowed from a descendant of Proto-Germanic *warōną (“to watch; protect”). Cognate with Veps varaita.

parole.significato: to churn, swirl about, mill, swell (to move rapidly and repetitively with a rocking motion)
parole.testo: Usually considered sound-symbolic; alternatively possibly borrowed from a descendant of Proto-Germanic *wellaną (compare Old Norse vella (“to boil; well up”)) and derived with + -oa.

From Proto-Finnic *aivan (an instructive singular, compare ihan), probably borrowed from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Háywas, or alternatively from Proto-Germanic *aiwaz (“long time”). Cognate with Votic aiva (“always”) and Estonian aiva (“always”).
From Proto-Finnic *aukko (compare Estonian auk, Votic aukko), either derived from the same root as avata, aukea, or alternatively proposed to be a borrowing from Proto-Germanic *augô (“eye”).
Borrowed either from North Germanic (compare Old Norse enda) or from Middle Low German ende, in either case ultimately from Proto-Germanic *anþi. Compare Estonian ent (“but”).

Probably from Proto-Finnic *hagastadak, derived from unattested *haka (“quarrel, legal matter”) (earlier *šaka), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *sakō. Alternatively, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian žósti (“to say”)). Related to Karelian hoastoa.

parole.significato: fluff of wool; tuft of wool to be spun; rolag
parole.testo: From hahtu + -va, the shorter form being derivative of either Proto-Finnic *hapci (thus from earlier *haptu) or alternatively a borrowing from Proto-Germanic *hazdaz (thus from earlier *haštu).

parole.significato: swidden; farmland that is produced using the slash and burn technique
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *halmëh, borrowed from either Proto-Germanic *halmaz or alternatively Proto-Baltic [Term?] (whence Lithuanian želmuo). Cognate with Estonian ale, Karelian halmeh, Ludian halmeh and Veps haumeh.

parole.significato: skirt, base, lap (part of a dress or robe, etc., that hangs below the waist)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hëlma (compare Estonian hõlm), possibly borrowed either from Baltic (compare Lithuanian šelmuo (“ridge (of a roof)”)) or from Proto-Germanic *helmaz (“protective covering”) (compare Old English helm (“helmet, protection, covering”)).
From Proto-Finnic *helbeh, borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (whence Old High German helwa, helawa), or alternatively a more recent Germanic borrowing.

A genitive or instructive singular form of *hiema, which could be from Proto-Finnic *hëëma-, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *sēmô through earlier *šeema(n) (in which case the word is a doublet of siemen), or alternatively derived from hieta through irregular suffix substitution. However, neit
From Proto-Finnic *huilu, probably onomatopoeic or alternatively (from earlier *šuilu and) borrowed from Proto-Germanic *sweglō.

From Proto-Finnic *huima (compare Estonian uim, Ingrian huima), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (compare Old Norse svíma (“to faint, to swoon”)) or Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare Old Norse hvima (“to be confused”)); for sense, compare huimata. Alternatively, possibly akin to huikea (comp

From Proto-Finnic *hämärä, derived from a root hämä-, which may be possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (compare Icelandic sámur) or from Baltic. Related to Estonian hämar, Karelian hämärä, Livonian ämār, Veps hämär and Votic hämäre.

parole.significato: group, cluster, band; crowd (of people) (number of things or persons, especially a rather large and unorganized one)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *joukko, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *jaukiją or from older Proto-Indo-European *yewg- (see the Proto-Finnic entry for more).

Probably from Proto-Finnic *kalppa, borrowed by metathesis from Proto-Germanic *glapa- (whence Icelandic glapp (“misfortune”) and Old Norse glap (“fornication, impropriety”)). Alternatively, possibly akin to kalpea, with development like “pale” → “ugly” → “bad”. In either case, with + -ten.

From Proto-Finnic *kamala (compare Ingrian kamala, Karelian kamala, Votic kamalõ), possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hamalaz. Alternatively, possibly related to Erzya кама- (kama-) in камажа (kamaža, “bad”).

parole.significato: to limb, delimb (to remove the branches of a tree)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *karcidak, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skardijaną, or alternatively from Baltic (compare Lithuanian skardyti).

parole.significato: bow, prow (front of a boat or ship)
parole.testo: Possibly from Proto-Finnic *këula, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skeulą (“shelter”) or alternatively Proto-Germanic *keulaz (“ship”). Alternatively from Proto-Finnic *këpla, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *geblą.
From Proto-Finnic *kiivas, borrowed from Proto-Baltic *gīˀwás or alternatively from Proto-Germanic *kwiwaz (“lively, quick”), both from Proto-Indo-European *gʷih₃wós.
From Proto-Finnic *kura (“dirt, mud”) (compare Estonian kura), possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *gurą or alternatively from Proto-Uralic *kura (“dirt, mud”).

parole.significato: to strangle, choke, throttle (constrict someone's windpipe so that they cannot breathe)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kurgistadak, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *kwirkijaną. Alternatively, and less likely, related to kuroa.

From Proto-Finnic *lakja (compare Estonian lai, Livonian laigā, Votic ladʹdʹõ), borrowed from Germanic, either Proto-Germanic *flakją (compare German flach) or alternatively *lēgijaz (compare laakea).

parole.significato: sect (offshoot of a larger religion sharing at least some unorthodox beliefs)
parole.testo: Partly from Proto-Finnic *lahko (compare Estonian lahk, Livonian lǭ’gõ, Veps lahk), borrowed either from Proto-Germanic *slagiz or Proto-Germanic *slahō. The original sense inherited from Finnic is “split log”, which is found only in some eastern Finnish dialects in the form laahko. Partly borrowed

Borrowed from Late Old Swedish lakan, from Late Old Norse lak, lakan, from Old Saxon lakan, from Proto-Germanic *lakaną (“sheet, cloth”); alternatively directly from either Old Saxon lakan, or an older Germanic loan.

parole.significato: paralysis, depression (state of being unable to act)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lama (compare Estonian lamama (“to lie down”), Ludian lama, Votic lama), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *lamaz (“lame, withered; defective”). Alternatively related to Moksha лама (lama) and Erzya ламо (lamo, “many”), although the semantic shift is problematic.

From Proto-Finnic *lauha, of unclear further etymology; either related to Erzya лавшо (lavšo, “weak”), or alternatively borrowed from Proto-Germanic *lausaz (compare Swedish lös) or Proto-Germanic *hlāwaz (variant of *hlēwaz).

parole.significato: board (long, wide and thin piece of sawn timber)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lauta (compare Estonian laud (“table”)), most likely borrowed from Proto-Baltic *plauˀtá (compare Latvian plàukts, Lithuanian plaũtas (“shelf”)), or alternatively from Proto-Germanic *flauþī (compare Norwegian Nynorsk flauta (“crossbeam in sleigh”)). The word has also been borrowe

parole.significato: to sail (to move briskly and gracefully through the air)
parole.testo: Possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *glīdaną, either as an old borrowing (into Proto-Finnic *liitädäk) or a more recent one (such as from Swedish glida). Cognate with Karelian liiteä.

parole.significato: A recurring pain in limbs; could mean several diseases, most probably gout.
parole.testo: luu (“bone”) + valo (“pain (archaic)”), latter part from Proto-Finnic *valo (“pain”), either borrowed from Proto-Germanic *kwalō or less likely from *valo (“light”).
From Proto-Finnic *mëtu, borrowed either from Proto-Balto-Slavic *medú or alternatively Proto-Germanic *meduz. Cognate with Estonian mõdu, Võro mõdu and Votic mõtu.
From Proto-Finnic *mura, probably from the same Proto-Uralic *mura- (“to break”) as murtaa, or alternatively from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (compare Icelandic mor).

parole.significato: ant (insect of the family Formicidae); (in the plural) the family Formicidae
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *muurahainën, borrowed either from Proto-Germanic *miurijǭ (compare Swedish myra), or from its source Proto-Indo-European *morwi- (compare Russian мураве́й (muravéj), Ukrainian мура́ха (muráxa), Polish mrówka). Contains a diminutive -(i)nen.
From Proto-Finnic *napa, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?], or alternatively and less likely from Proto-Germanic *nabō, but in either case ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₃nebʰ- (“navel”).
Either napa + kaira, formed after Proto-Norse *ᚾᚨᛒᛟᚷᚨᛁᛉᚨᛉ (*nabogaiʀaʀ) (from Proto-Germanic *nabōgaizaz), or directly borrowed from it.

parole.significato: rhinitis, "sniffles" (inflammation of the mucous membranes of the nose, leading to a runny or congested nose)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nuha, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *snuzaz (whence Swedish snor) or alternatively, from Proto-Germanic *hnuzô (whence Icelandic hnerri).
From Proto-Finnic *noodëh (albeit without any known Finnic cognates), either borrowed from Baltic (compare Latvian znots) or alternatively from Proto-Germanic *knōdiz.

Possibly borrowed from Middle Low German ovel, ovele, from Proto-Germanic *ubilaz. Alternatively related to dialectal evelä, Estonian õel (“wicked, cruel, savage, evil, mean”) and Votic õjõla (Pummala).
From Proto-Finnic *parta, borrowed from either Proto-Baltic *bardā́ˀ, Proto-Germanic *bardaz or Proto-Slavic *bordà, in any case ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *bʰardʰéh₂.

From Proto-Finnic *peijeh + -as, either from Proto-Indo-Iranian *paHiyas (“libation”) or alternatively and less likely from Proto-Germanic *faigijaz (“fey, doomed to die”), compare Old Norse feigr (“near to death”). Cognate with Estonian peied (“wake”).

parole.significato: goblin, hobgoblin, gnome, gremlin (mythical man-like creature, often depicted hairy, tailed and mischievous)
parole.testo: From older peikkoi, from Proto-Finnic *peikoi, *peiko (reshaped later with -kko; compare Estonian peig (“bridegroom”)), deriving either from Proto-Germanic *faihaz (“hostile, criminal”), *faigijaz (“fey”), or alternatively from a lost Baltic cognate (inexact parallels include Lithuanian paikas (“stu

parole.significato: sail; (colloquial) rag, sheet (piece of fabric attached to a boat and arranged such that it causes the wind to drive th…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *purjëh, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *buriz (“favourable wind”), or alternatively and less likely from Baltic (compare Lithuanian burė, Latvian bura). The Baltic words have also sometimes been proposed to be Finnic loans.

parole.significato: stripe, band (long strip of a colour or material)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *raidō, originally referring to a trail or track left behind while riding. Association with raita (etymology 2) has also been proposed. Cognate with Northern Karelian raita. Related to raide, either a derivative or a parallel loan from the same
From Proto-Finnic *rak'ëntadak, either borrowed from Proto-Germanic *rakjaną or inherited from Proto-Finno-Ugric *rakkɜ-.
From Proto-Finnic *rampa, borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *krampaz (“curved”), or from Proto-Baltic [Term?]. If the former, doublet of kremppa.

parole.significato: shore, strand, coast (the border of a body of water and land in general)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ranta (compare Estonian rand, Veps rand), borrowed from either Proto-Norse [script needed] (*stranða), Proto-Germanic *strandō (compare Swedish strand (“beach”)) or from Proto-Baltic *kranta (compare Lithuanian krantas (“beach, shore”)).

From Proto-Finnic *rindeh, probably from rinta (“chest, breast”) + -e, or alternatively (if from Proto-Finnic *rindek) possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (whence Norwegian strind (“strip, half, row, edge”) or rind (“esker, stripe in cloth”)).
From Proto-Finnic *roodëh, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (whence Old Norse tróð (“thatch, roof beam, rafter”)). Alternatively, possibly from ruoto + -e.
Probably borrowed from Middle Low German brôk with + -e; alternatively, an older borrowing from Proto-Germanic *brōks (implying Proto-Finnic *rook'ëh).

parole.significato: to sip, to drink, to toss off (have a drink)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rüüp'ät'äk. Cognate to Estonian rüüpama. Possibly onomatopoeic; alternatively a loan from Proto-Germanic *dreupaną.
Borrowed from Old Swedish sagh, or possibly already from Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare maha), ultimately from Proto-Germanic *sagō.

parole.significato: a handle for carrying, particularly one that is relatively thin but stiff, e.g. made of metal wire or another similar m…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sanka, possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *ćanka (compare Erzya сянго (śango)) and borrowed from Indo-Iranian, or alternatively possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *stangō.

parole.significato: large, big, great (of considerable size or extent)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *suuri, borrowed either from Proto-Germanic *stūraz or from Proto-Indo-Iranian *stʰuHrás (see the Proto-Finnic entry for more).
From Proto-Finnic *tarbit'ak. Equivalent to tarve (“need”) + -ita or alternatively, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *þarbāną + -ita. Cognate with Ingrian tarvita and Karelian tarvita.

parole.significato: to meet (come face to face with)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tabat'ak, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *dabaną. Cognate with Ingrian tavata, Karelian tavata, Votic tavatõ, Estonian tabama, Ludian tabada, Livonian ta’bbõ (“to guess, to solve a riddle”). Alternatively, sometimes compared with Erzya тавадомс (tavadoms), Udmurt тупаны (tu
From Proto-Finnic *tërva, borrowed from either Proto-Baltic *dérwa or Proto-Germanic *terwą, but in either case ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *dérw-o-m, from *dóru (“wood”).
From Proto-Finnic *tuhma, possibly either from Proto-Finno-Permic *tušma or borrowed from Proto-Germanic *dusmaz.

parole.significato: thwart (seat across a boat on which a rower may sit)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tukto, either from Proto-Uralic *tuktɜ (“cross-beam”) (compare Hungarian tat (“stern (of a ship)”), Komi-Zyrian тік (tik, “cross wood, cross bar”) and Tym Southern Selkup тати (tati, “thwart (of a ship”)), or alternatively borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (compare Old Norse þo

parole.significato: A tuft of grass or other plants.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tup'as (compare Karelian tuvas, Ludian tubaz, Veps tupaz), possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *þūbaz (compare Icelandic þúfa, Swedish tuva) or from Indo-Iranian (see the Proto-Finnic entry for more).
From Proto-Finnic *vakja, borrowed either from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian vadzis (“crook, hook”), Lithuanian vagis) or alternatively from Proto-Germanic *wagjaz (compare English wedge).
Possibly from Proto-Finnic *vaanidak, probably borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *wēnijaną, or alternatively possibly cognate with Erzya and Moksha ваномс (vanoms, “to look”).
From Proto-Finnic *vaat'ëk, probably borrowed from Germanic, possibly from Northwest Proto-Germanic *wādiz, or alternatively a more recent borrowing (compare Old Norse váð). Displaced sopa.

parole.significato: to demand, insist, call for, order
parole.testo: Probably borrowed either from Proto-Norse [Term?] (from Proto-Germanic *wadjōną (“to wager, to pledge”)) or alternatively from Proto-Norse [Term?] (from Proto-Germanic *kwadjaną (“to greet”)). However, the -aa- (as opposed to short -a-) seems difficult to explain. Compare Karelian vuatie.
From Proto-Finnic *vaha, borrowed either from Proto-Germanic *wahsą, from Proto-Baltic *vakša (compare Latvian vasks), or all three are from a substrate language.
Possibly borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *swinþaz (for *þ > *h, compare huopa, murha), or alternatively onomatopoeic.

parole.significato: rent (payment made by a tenant or user of a service)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vookra (compare Karelian vuokra, Ludian vuogr; no more cognates are known), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wōkraz (“interest; usury, gain; increase”), or alternatively a more recent borrowing from Middle Low German wôker.

parole.significato: mother (woman in relation to her children)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *äitei (compare Southern Ostrobothnian äitee, äiree, Estonian eit (“old woman”), Võro äide, äidi, ääde (“mother, grandmother”)), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *aiþį̄ (compare Gothic 𐌰𐌹𐌸𐌴𐌹 (aiþei)) or from later Proto-Norse [script needed] (*aiðijōn). Attested since the time of Mikae

parole.significato: bank (edge of river or lake, especially a steep one)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *äpräs, borrowed either from Proto-Germanic *auraz or alternatively from *ōferaz. Cognate with Karelian äpräs, Livvi äbräs and Ludian äbräz.
